   - *Question:* How did responsibility for maintaining a public asset develop?
   - *Key Focus:* Trace maintenance responsibility for one bridge, pipe or public facility through dated standards, budgets and ownership changes; avoid judging condition from age alone. Evidence base: Trace dated origin records and subsequent interpretations. Case records: authorized inspection reports, asset registers, work orders, budgets and service interruption records.    - *Question:* Did a maintenance program improve the reliability measures it targeted?
   - *Key Focus:* Examine one documented maintenance program using inspections, completed work and service reliability; compare its results with stated targets. Evidence base: Read the original evaluation and its population, comparator, outcomes and limitations. Case records: authorized inspection reports, asset registers, work orders, budgets and service interruption records. Starting framework: FHWA transportation asset management guidance (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/asset/faq.cfm). Select and verify the dated underlying case sources before scripting..

   - *Question:* Whose inspection or upkeep work is missing from an infrastructure account?
   - *Key Focus:* Follow overlooked inspection, cleaning or repair work on one asset; use attributed accounts and published records without operational vulnerability details. Evidence base: Use attributable contribution records and consented participant accounts. Case records: authorized inspection reports, asset registers, work orders, budgets and service interruption records. Starting framework: FHWA transportation asset management guidance (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/asset/faq.cfm). Select and verify the dated underlying case sources before scripting..
4. **Infrastructure Maintenance: Understanding Infrastructure Maintenance**
   - *Question:* How do inspection, repair and renewal differ for one public asset?
   - *Key Focus:* Explain inspection, prioritization, repair and renewal through one public asset; distinguish routine maintenance from reconstruction or safety certification. Evidence base: Use primary definitions and a documented end-to-end example. Case records: authorized inspection reports, asset registers, work orders, budgets and service interruption records. Starting framework: FHWA transportation asset management guidance (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/asset/faq.cfm). Select and verify the dated underlying case sources before scripting..
5. **Infrastructure Maintenance: Tradeoffs in Infrastructure Maintenance**
   - *Question:* How do condition models classify the same asset's maintenance needs?
   - *Key Focus:* Compare condition and failure-risk models used for one asset class; examine assumptions, incomplete records and consequences of misclassification. Evidence base: Compare original methods, assumptions, measures and uncertainty. Case records: authorized inspection reports, asset registers, work orders, budgets and service interruption records. Starting framework: FHWA transportation asset management guidance (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/asset/faq.cfm). Select and verify the dated underlying case sources before scripting..

   - *Key Focus:* Reconstruct one maintenance-priority decision using inspection findings, budgets and service obligations; distinguish recorded reasons from assumed motives. Evidence base: Use decision records, assigned authority and attributed accounts. Case records: authorized inspection reports, asset registers, work orders, budgets and service interruption records. Starting framework: FHWA transportation asset management guidance (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/asset/faq.cfm). Select and verify the dated underlying case sources before scripting..

Evidence base: Build a dated before-and-after record without assuming causation. Case records: authorized inspection reports, asset registers, work orders, budgets and service interruption records. Starting framework: FHWA transportation asset management guidance (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/asset/faq.cfm). Select and verify the dated underlying case sources before scripting..

Evidence base: Trace the process, custody transfers and assigned responsibilities. Case records: authorized inspection reports, asset registers, work orders, budgets and service interruption records. Starting framework: FHWA transportation asset management guidance (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/asset/faq.cfm). Select and verify the dated underlying case sources before scripting..
